facts.content: The expected exchange rate moved to the right. To avoid generating expected capital gain or loss, the current exchange rate must be moved by the same amount. The curve will shift to the right. Only one curve can move. The curve will move to the left because net exports will decline. For any given level of the interest rate, net exports will be lower. The US moves to the left, causing output to fall. There is no movement in this case. If the Fed or the central bank does not react, the movement will not happen.

evidence.quote: And now the expected exchange rate moved to the right.

Well, in order not to generate expected capital gain or loss,
 Because I have to move the current exchange rate
 by the same amount.
And so that means this curve will shift to the right.
Only one can move.
It will move to the left, because net exports will decline.

Not for any given level of the interest rate,
 now we're going to have less net exports.
And therefore, the US moves to the left, so output falls.
But there's no movement here.

Unless the Fed reacts to that, the central bank reacts to that,
 it won't happen.
